results.title: Medium
results.content:
Seven months later, I’m not a Loom evangelist. I still keep OBS Studio as backup. I still complain about the subscription cost. I still roll my eyes when it crashes.

But I’m also not the same person who dismissed screen recording as “unnecessary complexity.” Sometimes the imperfect tool that your team actually uses beats the perfect tool that sits unused.

My rating: ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ (3/5) — Flawed but functional, frustrating but effective. [...] Don’t get me wrong — I had good reasons to be skeptical. The few times I’d tried Loom, it crashed mid-recording, produced laggy videos, and generally felt like paying $15/month to be frustrated.

But here’s the thing: sometimes being wrong is the best thing that can happen to your workflow.

## The Resistance Was Real [...] I’d been so focused on the tool’s technical flaws that I missed the bigger picture: the mindset shift from synchronous to asynchronous communication changes everything.

Sure, Loom has problems. But so does spending six hours a week in meetings that could’ve been videos. So does losing context in endless Slack threads. So does explaining the same process to five different people in five separate calls.

## The Honest Bottom Line
